subject: rstan: large fit size causes memory problems

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: rstan: large fit size causes memory problems
parts:
Hi,

Is there a possibility to eliminate warm up samples when transferring fit object from stan to r.  In order to use waic I have to expose log_lik and for relative large data sets it causes memory problems such as "cannot allocate vector of size 86 Kb". Data set has 4000 measurements, warm up=10000, iter=11000.

Thanks for any suggestions,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: large fit size causes memory problems
parts:
Jiqiang,

I am not sure it may be reproduced.  But it happened not once.  It usually occurs when fit object contains samples for multiple variables (such as log likelihood for a large data set) and warmup is sufficiently large (10000) and I forget to remove previous fit objects.  Al least for my purposes I am not really interested in warm up samples.  So I wonder if it is possible to specify in sampling function eliminate warm up samples before output to R.
Thank you,
Linas

No, there is not such an option in rstan.  The output form CmdStan does not include warmup by default.  So in this case using CmdStan might be an option for now.

Jiqiang

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: large fit size causes memory problems
parts:
Hi Linus,

I'm using rstan and use the following code to extract samples (excluding warmup) from a stanfit object ("fit"):

fitarray <- extract(fit, permuted = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE)

Luc
